{{short description|Mathematical concept}}
In [[abstract algebra|algebra]], a '''differential graded module''', or '''dg-module''', is a <math>\mathbb{Z}</math>-[[graded module]] together with a differential; i.e., a square-zero graded [[endomorphism]] of the [[module (mathematics)|module]] of degree 1 or −1, depending on the convention. In other words, it is a [[chain complex]] having a structure of a module, while a [[differential graded algebra]] is a chain complex with a structure of an [[algebra over a ring|algebra]].

In view of the module-variant of [[Dold–Kan correspondence]], the notion of an <math>\mathbb{N}_0</math>-graded dg-module is equivalent to that of a '''simplicial module'''; "[[equivalence of categories|equivalent]]" in the [[category theory|categorical]] sense; see {{sectionlink||The Dold–Kan correspondence}} below.

== The Dold–Kan correspondence ==
Given a [[commutative ring]] ''R'', by definition, the [[category (mathematics)|category]] of [[simplicial module]]s are [[simplicial object]]s in the [[category of modules|category of ''R''-modules]]; denoted by '''''s'''''Mod<sub>''R''</sub>. Then '''''s'''''Mod<sub>''R''</sub> can be identified with the category of differential graded modules which vanish in negative degrees via the [[Dold-Kan correspondence]].<ref>{{harvnb|Fresse|2017}}{{page needed|date=January 2017}}</ref><!--The category of differential modules over a ring ''R'' coincides with the category of modules over the ring <math>R[\epsilon]</math> of dual numbers over ''R''.(Cartan-Eilenberg)-->
